Apex Industrial Machinery Corp. - Q4 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Industrial Machinery Corp. Q4 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to request through the phone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson (VP of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Industrial Machinery Corp.'s results for the Q4 2024. Joining me on today's call are Mike Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; John Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Operating Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mike Reynolds.

Mike Reynolds (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Apex Industrial Machinery Corp.'s performance for the Q4 2024. We've made significant progress on several fronts, and I'd like to highlight a few key achievements. We posted strong total revenue of $1.48 billion, up 14% year-over-year with robust organic growth outpacing the industry. Our backlog reached $2.85 billion, up 22% from last year, providing excellent visibility. We're guiding revenue higher for next quarter and full year, alongside operating margin expansion. End markets show solid near-term growth of 5-8% and accelerating to 8-11% medium term across aerospace, semis, and energy. Capital expenditures are ramping strategically to fuel capacity and tech upgrades. We've boosted our dividend with a compelling yield, and executed aggressively on share repurchases to drive shareholder value.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to John Harlan to provide more detail on our financial results.

John Harlan (CFO):
Thank you, Mike. Good morning, everyone. Turning to our financial performance, Apex Industrial Machinery Corp. reported $1.48 billion in revenue for the Q4 2024, representing a 14% increase year-over-year, or 12% on an organic basis excluding our recent acquisition of Precision Robotics Solutions. This marks our ninth straight quarter of double-digit growth, outpacing the broader industrial machinery index. For the full fiscal year 2024, total revenue climbed to $5.62 billion, up 15% year-over-year, with organic growth of 13%. Volume drove about 9 points of that, from a 22% surge in orders for next-gen CNC machining centers and collaborative robots key to reshoring in semiconductors and EVs. Pricing added 4 points via 5-7% annual increases held firm despite easing raw materials.

By segment, Automation & Robotics, now 42% of revenue at $2.36 billion annually, grew 22%, powered by AI data center capex and our ApexFlex modular arms integrating with Siemens MindSphere for predictive maintenance. Heavy Equipment, 35% at $1.97 billion, rose 11% on 18% aftermarket parts growth. Precision Components, 23% at $1.29 billion, advanced 9%, with aerospace strength offsetting softer autos.

Regionally, North America at 52% or $2.92 billion grew 18% on CHIPS Act fab demand. EMEA at 28% or $1.57 billion up 12%, APAC 20% or $1.13 billion surged 14% on EV battery deals with CATL and BYD.

Gross margin was 32.5%, driven by mix shift to high-margin automation, supply chain efficiencies, and pricing. Operating expenses were controlled at $450 million, resulting in operating income of $285 million. Net income was $210 million, or $4.85 adjusted EPS.

Now, let's dive deeper into backlog value and expected conversion. As of Q4 end, total backlog stood at $2.85 billion, up 22% year-over-year from $2.33 billion and 8% sequentially from Q3. Trailing 12-month book-to-bill is 1.28x, ahead of peers. Semiconductor and electronics backlog up 35% YoY to $1.12 billion (39% of total), tied to CHIPS Act and AI capex. Aerospace and defense steady at $850 million (up 15%), energy transition up 42% to $880 million on IRA and offshore wind.

North America leads at 58% ($1.65 billion, +28% YoY), EMEA 24% ($685 million, +12%), APAC 18% ($465 million, +18%). Conversion timeline is 9-11 months weighted average, 65% within 12 months, tightened by SAP AI forecasting cutting lead times 22%, $150 million capacity adds in Greenville, and digital twins shaving 4-6 weeks off commissioning. High-margin custom orders now 55% of book, supporting 18-20% EBITDA margins. Q4 conversion hit $750-800 million at 85% utilization.

Turning to revenue guidance. For Q1 2025, we guide $1.35 billion to $1.42 billion, up 9-14% YoY, sequential 5-11%. North America 48% mix up on HyperForge CNC for Tesla-like battery lines and data center cooling, post-Ohio expansion. EMEA flattish on energy costs but gaining in eco-hydraulics for Airbus. APAC mid-single digits on semi wafer handling for TSMC/Samsung. Book-to-bill 1.15x, gross margins to 32.5%.

Full-year 2025 outlook raised to $5.45-5.65 billion, 12-17% growth over 2024. Precision Machining $2.85-2.95 billion (14-19%), Automation $1.55-1.65 billion (18-25%), Heavy Equipment $1.05-1.10 billion (flat to +5%). North America 47%, EMEA 27%, APAC 26%. 35% revenue now IoT-embedded, targeting digital transformation market.

On operating margins, Q1 guide 14.0-15.0%, up sequentially on automation seasonality. Tailwinds: Industry 4.0 digital twins yielding 3-5% productivity, steel/aluminum down 15% hedged 80%, 4% pricing. Headwinds: copper up 10%, Europe mix. Full-year 14.5-15.5%, raised from prior, on $5.0-5.1 billion revenue. Drivers: 35% growth in E-Motion hybrids, $150 million savings via lean/ERP, capex 4.5%. North America 17-18%, APAC 16%.

Shifting to end-market outlook. Near-term through 2025, 5-7% growth 2024, 6-8% 2025, from CAPEX recovery, book-to-bill 1.15x, $4.2 billion backlog (65% next 12 months). Aerospace (35% revenue) 8-10% on Boeing/Airbus ramps, NDAA defense. Automotive (25%) 4-6%, EV/hybrids exploding. Semis (15%) 12-15% on TSMC/Intel fabs. Energy (20%) 5-7%, renewables accelerant. General industrial 3-5%. North America 7-9%, APAC 8-10%.

Medium-term 2026-2028, 8-11% CAGR to $1.2T TAM. Aerospace 10-12%, automotive 9-11% EVs, semis 14-16% AI, energy 10-13% LNG/renewables. Investments: $450 million in SmartForge IoT platform (live 40% machines, $200M recurring by 2028), electrification hybrids, sustainability. Mexico greenfield, India JV.

Capital expenditures remain core. FY2024 $525 million, 4.2% of TTM revenue, 12.5% incremental ROIC >8.2% WACC, up 15% YoY despite inflation. 2025 guide $650-700 million, 4.5-4.8% revenue, 24-33% up, from $850 million op cash flow, net debt/EBITDA 1.2x.

Priorities: Growth 55% ($360-385M): NA $150M Greenville CNC +25% for CHIPS semis (50 Haas/DMG mills), APAC $110M Suzhou EV lines for CATL/BYD, Europe $55M Toulouse aero MRO. Tech/digital 30% ($195-210M): $120M Siemens MindSphere IoT (28% downtime cut), $50M EOS 3D printers, $45M solar/hydrogen (25% Scope 1 cut). Maintenance 15% ($100M): overhauls, cybersecurity.

IRRs 18-20% growth, 25%+ tech. Derisked modular, partners Siemens/Rockwell. Risks steel tariffs, upside reshoring PMI>50.

On dividend policy, announcing 7% hike to $0.78 quarterly, annualized $3.12, 2.9% yield at $108.50 close, top quartile vs. IR 2.1%, Cummins 2.8%. 28th year increase, 8.2% 10-year CAGR. 40-50% payout on $6.78 TTM adj EPS, 46% ratio. NA cash engine $1.2B YTD, EMEA/ APAC mixed. Aligns 40% returns, 35% organic like SC Industry 4.0, 25% M&A. FY24 FCF $2.1-2.3B capacity for more hikes.

Share repurchases: $750M authorization Feb 2024, executed $420M YTD, 8.2M shares at $51.22 avg, 56% done. Q3 $180M at $52.94. Opportunistic via 10b5-1 (60%) Goldman VWAP, blocks (40%). 20% EPS accretion, 11.2x EV/EBITDA discount to peers. NA FCF $300M+ funded 70%. Remaining $330M, $100-150M Q4. Enhances ROIC to 16.5%, 8-10% growth.

We remain committed to disciplined capital allocation and maximizing shareholder value. That covers the financials in detail.

Now, I'll hand over to David Patel, COO, for an operational update.

David Patel (COO):
Thank you, John. Operationally, we've optimized manufacturing processes, boosted supply chain efficiency through dual-sourcing and SAP digitization, and enhanced customer service with localized hubs. We're leveraging digital twins and AI analytics for excellence, mirroring Rockwell gains. Employee health and safety remains priority, with zero lost-time incidents this quarter amid expansions.

I'll turn the call over to Elena Vasquez, CTO, for our technology roadmap.

Elena Vasquez (CTO):
Thank you, David. We're driving innovation in AI, machine learning, robotics, and IoT for customers. Investments target predictive maintenance, operations optimization, product performance. Our new SmartForge platform is transforming the market, live on 40% machines, boosting uptime 25%, unlocking $200 million recurring software by 2028, with 30% energy savings in hybrids.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Ben Smith (JPMorgan):
Good morning. Can you discuss the long-term impact of the new SmartForge platform on your revenue and profitability?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Ben. SmartForge positions us at megatrend intersections, with digital twins and AI driving 25% OEM uptime gains, shifting 35% revenue to software-embedded high-margin products. Long-term, it targets $200 million recurring by 2028 from subscriptions, expanding ASP 8%, margins 150-200 bps via Industry 4.0. In semis and EVs, it's accelerating adoption like Siemens partners, supporting 10%+ organic growth and ROIC >20%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen (Goldman Sachs):
What are your expectations for revenue growth in the coming year?

John Harlan:
Good question, Lisa. For FY2025, we're guiding $5.45-5.65 billion, 12-17% growth, above prior, on $4.7 billion backlog up 22%, multi-year EV/semi awards. Organic 10-13%, led by automation 18-25%, North America reshoring. Seculars like 8% CAGR automation per McKinsey underpin outperformance.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Rivera with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Tom Rivera (Morgan Stanley):
Can you discuss your plans for expanding your global footprint?

Mike Reynolds:
Absolutely, Tom. We're investing $150 million Mexico greenfield for nearshoring, Suzhou EV expansions, Toulouse aero MRO, India JV for semis/renewables. Capacity +25% Greenville/Ohio, hedging tariffs dual-sourcing. APAC/NA focus captures 7-10% regional growth, with 70% NA content mitigating logistics.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Alex Kim (Barclays):
How are you managing rising energy costs?

David Patel:
Great question, Alex. We're tackling via $45 million electrification: retrofitting 200+ forklifts/AGVs with hydrogen fuel cells, 10MW Peoria solar aligning IRA credits, targeting 25% Scope 1 cut by 2027. Digital twins optimize throughput 3-5%, MindSphere IoT cuts downtime 28%. Europe energy surcharges offset by efficient servos, localized inventory.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes our Q&A.

Mike Reynolds:
Thank you for your questions and your interest in Apex Industrial Machinery Corp. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
